memo.verdict: Neutral; park. The record parks RWE (RWE-DE) at EUR 59.10 (2026-10-02) on return grounds, not on the gate: the modal return is 8.1 percent a year over eighteen months and 9.4 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The park rule (a D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability) finds nothing: management RA 3, E 1, BB 4 at A; business quality E 2, BB 2 at B; predictability RA 8, E 2, BB 4 at B; trackability RA 7, E 2, BB 4 at B. Conviction: medium on the business, high on the arithmetic. The case stays on the watch list because the business is one the record would own at the right price. Move to bullish and progress: a price at or below about EUR 45 to 50 with the path intact (three-year clearing price EUR 44.75 at 16.0x; eighteen-month clearing price EUR 50.5), or a change in the path large enough to clear the bar at today's price, which would need earnings two years beyond the three-year horizon near EUR 5.75 at 17.0x and which no file supports. Move to bearish: an RP5 draft return on equity below 7.0 percent, or FY2027 adjusted earnings per share guided below EUR 3.00 at the midpoint at the March 2027 results. One-line form: the right company at the wrong price.
case: - Thesis. RWE is a self-help case of the 'Major Corporate Change' kind with a demand tailwind behind it: a return-disciplined management spent 2025 and 2026 turning a merchant-exposed renewables developer into a three-pillar utility (offshore and onshore renewables under long contracts, flexible gas under capacity payments, a 55 percent pro-rata stake in the Amprion transmission grid from June 2026) whose earnings are mostly contracted or regulated, and the outputs have arrived in the statements, the guidance and the consensus. At EUR 59.10 the shares have paid for that change in advance.

- The change is internal first, external second, and real. Hurdle raised to over 8.5 percent, 9.9 percent achieved on projects sanctioned since early 2025; net investment EUR 42bn for 2026 to 2031 with EUR 7bn for German grids; Amprion bought at 1.07x asset base and funded by a EUR 4bn raise at EUR 54; what could not earn the hurdle sold (US offshore for USD 1.22bn, US distributed generation, Sweden, Poland; lignite closes by 31 March 2030). Five of twelve internal forces strong (strategy A, guidance A, perimeter A, acquisitions B, balance sheet B), meeting the screen rule of three. External tailwinds: demand (4.8 GW of long contracts at 20 to 35 percent above baselines; European data-centre capacity growing 21 percent a year), competition (oil majors and Orsted in retreat; AR7 cleared 14 percent real above AR6, RWE 6.9 of 8.4 GW), regulation (German capacity act passed with two 4.5 GW auctions on 8 September and 22 December 2026, payments capped at EUR 244/kW a year from 1 November 2031; UK contracts extended to 20 years; EUR 332m Dutch compensation paid; EUR 2.6bn lignite compensation confirmed). The one external headwind, solar cannibalisation of merchant capture prices (German solar capture 62 percent of baseload in 2024 from 97 percent in 2018), is hedged with batteries and contracting. Supply chain (transformer lead times 2.5 to 4.5 years, prices up 400 to 900 percent on 2020; vessels over 85 percent utilised) and the macro force (EUR 10/MWh of power price is about 5 percent of long-term earnings per share) are neutral at best. 'Change Forces' B.

- 'Financial Outputs' have arrived at every layer. H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA EUR 3,011m up 44 percent; adjusted earnings per share EUR 1.77 up 64 percent; FY2026 guidance raised 16 percent at the midpoint to EUR 2.95 on 28 July 2026; FY2026 consensus up 24.2 percent in twelve months to EUR 3.06. The same team, extended to June 2031, chose the pillar and the hurdle, acted, and operating metrics (10.3 GW under construction), statements and sell-side moved; the change has travelled all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain. Sell-side upgrades likely (B): three years of raising or beating guidance (FY2023 adjusted EBITDA EUR 8,378m against an upper bound of EUR 7,700m; FY2025 adjusted net income EUR 1.8bn beat consensus by 8 percent); a "sandbagger" habit; Redburn calls guidance "structurally conservative"; Jefferies notes spot power up to 41 percent above management's assumptions, worth EUR 0.17 of earnings per share; revision skew far above three to one. Goldilocks growth B: 13.7 percent a year to FY2028 on the record's path, 12.8 on consensus; 16.2 percent a year to FY2027. Staircase B: capacity auction results, a data-centre deal the chief executive is highly confident of before end-2026, Sofia full operation, Q3 results 2026-11-11, AR8; then FY2026 results in March 2027 with first grid-segment guidance, RP5 draft Q1 2027, Thor 2027.
counter_case: - In its strongest form, from the risks research and from Bernstein: the H1 2026 beat was a false friend. Strip the EUR 332m Dutch compensation and about EUR 100m of trading one-offs and Flexible Generation was weaker year on year on lower spreads. Capitalised interest of EUR 800m flatters reported earnings and reverses as projects commission. Asset lives were extended (solar to 35 years, batteries to 15) to lower depreciation. Free cash flow was EUR -7,048m for a single half-year. The grid is a quasi-financial asset RWE does not operate, bought at a premium to its 2025 carrying value, whose return is set by a regulator in 2027 (RWE assumes 8.0 percent; the gas draft set lower parameters), funded with a 10 percent equity issue that yields about 1 percent of earnings-per-share accretion in 2027 on Bernstein's arithmetic. The merchant third of the book faces structural price cannibalisation (near-zero-priced hours up 50 percent; Spanish solar at 58 percent of baseload). And the shares at the 73rd percentile of their own multiple, 24 percent above the sector, discount all of the bull case and none of this. The evidence is tangible and filings-backed: provisions EUR 9,957m for nuclear and mining, pensions EUR 4,662m. The Apollo joint venture that diluted Amprion ten months before the EUR 3.6bn consolidation is structurally inconsistent. The research names this the winning hypothesis under its competing-hypotheses discipline, and it is the archetype that fits: "near-term trading and compensation windfalls successfully mask long-term green return degradation".

- The second form, from the other side: this is a 'Compounder' the market has read correctly, and the right response is to own it at the full multiple because earnings will grow into it at 11 to 14 percent a year; holding at 17.0x gives 11.5 to 12.5 percent a year.
triggers: - Bullish and progress: price at or below about EUR 45 to 50 with the path intact (EUR 44.75 three-year clearing at 16.0x; EUR 50.5 eighteen-month; EUR 47.4 and EUR 53.6 at 17.0x); or a path change needing earnings two years beyond the three-year horizon near EUR 5.75 at 17.0x.

- Bearish: RP5 draft (Q1 2027) below 7.0 percent return on equity; FY2027 adjusted earnings per share guided below EUR 3.00 at the midpoint at the March 2027 results. Invalidate levels: RP5 final (Q3 2027) below 7.0 percent; FY2027 guided below EUR 3.00 at the midpoint.

- Alarm levels: German Cal-27 and Cal-28 forwards below EUR 52/MWh for two months; near-zero-price hours above 4 percent; 10-year Bund yields above 3.25 percent; Supply and Trading below zero in a quarter; RP5 draft return on equity below 8.0 percent; capitalised interest below EUR 600m in FY2027 or minorities above EUR 500m; a sustained move in the multiple below the ten-year median 14.0x; a flagship project slipping by more than a quarter; a transformer delay beyond four years or a vessel outage; achieved returns falling toward the hurdle.

- Dated steps: capacity auction results (8 September and 22 December 2026 auctions; unconfirmed as at 2026-10-02); a data-centre site deal before end-2026; Sofia full operation from September 2026; Q3 results 2026-11-11; AR8 results; FY2026 results March 2027 with first Regulated Grid Infrastructure guidance (EUR 450 to 500m); RP5 draft Q1 2027 and final Q3 2027; Thor 2027; Nordseecluster phase B 2028; US gas peakers 2029; audit chair's ten-year limit late 2026.

- Open: whether the mix shift covers the one-off roll-off in FY2027 (headline 8 percent on the record's path, about 24 percent on the one-off-free base); whether a second trading quarter goes negative; whether a second equity raise is needed (none mooted); whether the market re-files RWE as a utility (sector thematic pin D for 35 of 36); further Amprion stake talks and the Apollo buy-back option around 2032; AI capital-spending slowdown and defence crowding out green subsidy (not yet in the order book).

- Not read: the framework's live thematics file, the ticker's sidecar, the track-record and lessons files, the Wisdom Library; the four own-error fits are offered for those files to confirm or reject. Fifteen earlier files on the company (2026-05-22) held out.
